title: Strict principal reduction cones and their compatible cone comparisons
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\pi$, and $X$ any scheme. Put $R=\mathcal O_{E,X}=p_X^*\underline{\mathcal O_E}$, with the coefficient sheaves of [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use unbounded cochain complexes of $R$-module sheaves and the cone, shift and localization conventions of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For $n\ge1$ define $D_n(M)=\operatorname{Cone}(\pi^n:M\to M)$, with diagonal maps on chain maps, transition $D_{n+1}(M)\to D_n(M)$ given by $(x,y)\mapsto(x,\pi y)$, and coaugmentation $j_n:M\to D_n(M)$ given by $m\mapsto(m,0)$. This is a functorial strict model of the derived reduction tower of [sk-def-pe-derived-completion]: writing $K_n=K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_R(\mathcal O_E/\pi^n)_X$, regarded as an $R$-module object by restriction of scalars, there are isomorphisms $QD_n(M)\cong(QM)_n$ in $D(R)$, natural in $M$, carrying $QD_n$ of the transition to the canonical transition $K_{n+1}\to K_n$ and $Q(j_n)$ to the canonical reduction map $K\to K_n$. Each $D_n$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms and induces an additive exact endofunctor of $D(R)$. For a chain map $f:A\to B$ its cone comparison
$$D_n(\operatorname{Cone}(f))\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Cone}(D_n(f))$$
is $(b,a,b',a')\mapsto(b,b',a,-a')$ in the ordered coordinates $B^q,A^{q+1},B^{q+1},A^{q+2}$. The shift comparison $D_n(M[r])\xrightarrow{\sim}D_n(M)[r]$ is $(x,y)\mapsto(x,(-1)^r y)$ for every integer $r$. These comparisons are natural, commute with all tower transitions, preserve cone inclusions and the boundary after the shift comparison, and carry $j_{\operatorname{Cone}(f)}$ to the cone map of $(j_A,j_B)$ and $j_{M[r]}$ to $j_M[r]$.

proof.text: Construct the prescribed uniformizer endomorphism explicitly by pointwise multiplication on continuous-map sections, as in det-pe-derived-nakayama-resolution, and prove its module linearity and section formula. Construct the strict endofunctor as the standard scalar mapping cone with diagonal cone maps, its transition as cone.map(d,id), and its unit as cone.inr. Functoriality is cone-map composition; the power identity follows functorially from multiplication of regular-module endomorphisms. The fixed degreewise biproduct coordinates prove all strict map and unit formulas.

proof.text: A scalar-cone morphism induced by a quasi-isomorphism is the third component of a morphism of distinguished scalar-cone triangles whose first two components are isomorphisms. The derived-category two-out-of-three lemma makes its localization invertible, hence the cone map is a quasi-isomorphism.

proof.text: For the two scalar rows and f, construct a double-cone chain isomorphism by the four-coordinate permutation (b,a,bprime,aprime) to (b,bprime,a,-aprime). Its inverse uses the same permutation and sign. Verify the differential by the two cone projections and additivity. The same projections prove naturality, compatibility with scalar transitions, cone inclusions and the cone map of coaugmentations. Construct coherent all-integer shift isomorphisms from the standard mappingCone.shiftIso and the scalar transformation commuting with termwise shifts; verify the zero and addition laws and the stated signed coordinates. The boundary equation follows by the cone projections, including the negative sign of its shifted component.
